question: Should OpenClaw accept `currentTokenCount` plus these SDK token-budget helpers as a stable public ContextEngine/plugin SDK contract now, or fold token budgeting into the broader assemble metadata design tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82137?
rationale: The patch changes public plugin API and SDK exports that third-party context engines may compile against, while the broader assemble metadata design remains unsettled.

options.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Fixes
options.body: Approve `currentTokenCount` as a separate backward-compatible API, but require the count-alignment fix, SDK baseline regeneration, and redacted live behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Fold Into Broader RFC
options.body: Pause this PR and land token counts together with the broader provenance/internal-event assemble metadata design.

options.title: Keep Helpers Private For Now
options.body: Allow internal runtime plumbing but remove or defer the SDK helper exports until maintainers settle the public plugin API shape.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Fixes
recommendation.body: Approve `currentTokenCount` as a separate backward-compatible API, but require the count-alignment fix, SDK baseline regeneration, and redacted live behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned and have the strongest recent merged history on the affected context-engine token-budget path.
